title: Substitution coherence of the interpretation of the term calculus for the free cornering of a monoidal category
author: Chad Nester, Niels Voorneveld
work: A Simple Categorical Calculus of Interacting Processes
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Lemma 3.7 (source label 'lem:substitution-coherent'), the substitution coherence of the authors' interpretation of the term calculus: the interpretation of a let-term whose variables are assigned a tuple of values equals the interpretation of the term in which those values have been substituted, whenever the substitution makes sense. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete structural induction over the whole syntax of the calculus rather than a one-line rewriting: it treats the value case and the nested let case separately, expands the interpretation through the cornering operation and the monoidal product, uses the functoriality of the free cornering to move the tuple of values through the tensor product, and closes the let case by applying the induction hypothesis to each of the branches before reassembling the tuple. Establishing coherence between a denotational interpretation and a syntactic substitution relation is the central well-definedness obligation of a categorical calculus, and it is research-level categorical semantics rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.
